questions.q: Where had the Rat been while the Mole was out on the river with companions?
choices: Visiting the Otter
Visiting the Badger
Rowing up to Toad Hall
Fishing alone at the weir
questions.evidence: keep a engagement of long standing with Otter

questions.q: What trouble had come to the Otter family?
choices: Little Portly was missing
Their riverside house had flooded
Otter had been caught in a trap
Weasels had stolen their boat

questions.q: How did the Mole first react to the news that Portly was missing?
choices: He didn't worry, since Portly always turned up
He burst into tears and could not stop crying
He ran off at once to search the whole river
He blamed Otter for being so careless with him
questions.evidence: He's always straying off and getting lost, and turning up again

questions.q: Why was Otter so worried about the weir?
choices: Portly had not yet learned to swim very well
Portly was terribly afraid of loud rushing noises
The weir had just been rebuilt and was unsafe
Weasels and stoats had moved in near the weir
questions.evidence: young Portly hasn't learnt to swim very well yet

questions.q: Why did Otter keep watch every night at the old ford?
choices: It was Portly's favourite spot, where Otter taught him to swim
It was the only safe place to cross the river for miles
Portly had been seen there last by the Mole and the Rat
It was close to Otter's home and easy to watch from
questions.evidence: it was there he gave Portly his first swimming-lesson

questions.q: Why did the Mole suggest getting the boat out in the middle of the night?
choices: He could not bear to go to bed and do nothing
He wanted to catch fish by the light of the moon
He wanted to row up and visit Toad Hall
He was too hot to sleep and wanted a cool swim
questions.evidence: it will be better than going to bed and doing NOTHING

questions.q: The moon rose "with slow majesty." What does "majesty" mean here?
choices: Grand, stately beauty
Nervous, trembling shaking
Great speed and hurry
A dim, cloudy colour
questions.evidence: the moon lifted with slow majesty

questions.q: What did the friends do after the moon rose?
choices: Tied up the boat and searched hedges, trees and ditches
Went home to bed and planned to search in the morning
Rowed to the ford to sit up with Otter all night
Rowed straight to the weir and waited there quietly
questions.evidence: patiently explored the hedges, the hollow trees

questions.q: What did the Rat suddenly hear as dawn approached?
choices: Distant piping music
Portly crying for help
A dog barking far off
Church bells ringing
questions.evidence: the thin, clear, happy call of the distant piping

questions.q: At first, what did the Mole say he could hear?
choices: Only the wind in the reeds and rushes
A bird singing in a willow tree
The roar of the weir far ahead
Otter calling out for Portly
questions.evidence: but the wind playing in the reeds and rushes and osiers

questions.q: The Rat was "entranced" and "spellbound" by the music. What do these words mean?
choices: So delighted he was completely held by it
Bored and sleepy after the long night
Angry and upset at being kept awake
Confused and quite lost in the dark wet meadows
questions.evidence: Entranced, he was silent for a long space, spellbound.

questions.q: Where did the music lead the two friends?
choices: To a small island in the middle of the weir
To the gates of Toad Hall on the river
To the dark edge of the Wild Wood
Back to the Rat's house on the bank

questions.q: On the island the Mole felt a great "awe." What is awe?
choices: Deep wonder and respect, with a little fear
Plain boredom after waiting all night in the cold boat
Hunger after a long night of rowing
Anger at being tricked by the music
questions.evidence: the Mole felt a great Awe fall upon him

questions.q: Where was Portly when the Mole saw the Friend and Helper?
choices: Sleeping between the Helper's hooves
Swimming happily in the pool below the weir
Caught in a trap set by a poacher
Hiding inside a hollow willow tree
questions.evidence: nestling between his very hooves, sleeping soundly

questions.q: What gift did the kindly demi-god give the animals as the breeze touched their faces?
choices: Forgetfulness, so the memory would not spoil their joy
A set of pan-pipes, so that they could play the music too
The power to hear that wonderful music forever
A safe path home through the meadows at dawn

questions.q: How did Portly feel after he woke up and searched the island?
choices: He cried bitterly because he could not find someone
He was proud of his big adventure on the island
He was angry at the Rat and the Mole for waking him
He was hungry and asked them for breakfast

questions.q: How did Rat and Mole return Portly to his father?
choices: They set him on the tow-path and watched him run to Otter
They carried him all the way home to Otter's house
They left him on the island and went to fetch Otter
They took him home to the Rat's house first for a hot breakfast
questions.evidence: set him on his legs on the tow-path

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Rat and Mole are led to lost Portly by a kindly Helper
Toad escapes from prison and buys a new motor-car
The Mole gets lost in the snowy Wild Wood and is rescued
The Rat decides to leave the River and go to sea
